correctness.rationale: Poisson thinning turns Bernoulli decisions at exponential run-end times into independent reset and flip clocks. A common-reset coupling proves uniqueness and an exponential age construction identifies the stationary law. The signed geometric excursion sum yields a rational characteristic transform, inverted exactly into positive half-line exponentials with full normalization and endpoint cases. Direct integration gives occupancy, mean and their strict thresholds; algebraic equality D²-[c-v(1-2theta)]²=4 theta(1-theta)v(c+v) proves positivity. The packaged deterministic checker reproduced 6255 checks including truncated excursion series, matrix resolvent, exact rational sign implication and boundaries; these finite checks supplement the analytical proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary paper gives an integral-defined stationary density (equations 41-42) and explicitly notes lack of a closed-form evaluation (Remark 15(iii)). It gives the first moment but not the explicit two-half-line exponential density, sign occupancy or exact mean-majority disagreement classification. Evans and Majumdar (2018) give a symmetric law under symmetric initial velocity and distinct velocity resets, so do not imply arbitrary asymmetric deterministic positive-velocity reset coefficients. A 2023 geometric-clock telegraph model uses nonexponential intertimes/external resets. Actual targeted research-record and literature searches found no dominating exact formulation, though a general two-state Markov-additive fluid/resolvent identity could yield it; global historical uniqueness is not certified.

value.rationale: The 2026 primary model motivated the unknown closed stationary local-time integral: this result evaluates it explicitly for all exponential parameters, giving two different decay rates and masses. The exact division between negative mean and negative majority is mathematically natural and creates a nonempty strict disagreement region, enabling tail-risk vs typical-sign analysis. The result covers the full three-parameter shape family and both probability boundary regimes, rather than a reparameterized textbook special case or arbitrary finite instance.
